# ChalkSmith — Prioritised Implementation Plan (proposal for review)

ChalkSmith is an independently written, Apache-2.0, cross-platform whiteboard.
It is not a clone of Microsoft Whiteboard's code or assets. It interoperates
by reading the documented-by-observation export format.

## Ground rules (clean room)

- Public repo contains **only** original code, the observed-behaviour docs, and
  **synthetic** fixtures written by hand or generated by our own scripts.
- Never commit: `original/` (proprietary package copy), anything from
  WebView2 caches, real exports, or derived evidence (`private/`). Both
  directories are git-ignored, in `.gitignore` and in `.git/info/exclude`.
- No Microsoft CSS, textures, icons, fonts, or strings. The importer drops the
  `<style>` block, and textures are substituted.
- Microsoft implementation code (host IL, cached web-app JS) is not read for
  implementation purposes.

## What can be recreated on Windows, macOS, and Linux (Q4)

All of the core whiteboard is reproducible with open technology. None of it
depends on Microsoft services:

| Feature | Recreatable | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Infinite canvas, pan/zoom | Yes | |
| Pen with pressure → variable width outline | Yes | Pointer Events give pressure/tilt on all three OSes (via the platform webview) |
| Highlighter, eraser (stroke and partial), lasso select, group | Yes | |
| Images, PDF insert as page images | Yes | PDF via pdf.js (Apache-2.0) |
| Text boxes, sticky notes, shapes, connectors | Yes | Not needed for import MVP |
| Export PNG / SVG / PDF | Yes | |
| Import Whiteboard Full Export ZIP | Yes | Ink + images now; other types later |
| Real-time collaboration | Later | CRDT (Yjs/Automerge) plus a self-hostable relay; no Microsoft dependency |
| Microsoft sign-in, Teams/OneDrive integration, cloud boards | **No / out of scope** | |
| Textured "galaxy/rainbow" pens | Original equivalents only | |

## Stack (decided 2026-10-16: TypeScript core + Tauri)

- **Core library (TypeScript, no DOM dependency):** document model, `.chalk`
  read/write, Whiteboard importer, stroke outline generation, hit-testing.
  Runs in Node (CLI, tests) and the app.
- **App shell: Tauri 2.** Uses the system webview (WebView2 / WKWebView /
  WebKitGTK), produces small installers, and gives native file dialogs.
  Rendering is Canvas 2D for ink (fast) with SVG export.
- Alternatives considered: Electron is simpler but much heavier; Avalonia/.NET
  is a good native fit but would mean a second renderer for web/export.
- Native file format `.chalk`: a ZIP holding `manifest.json` (format
  version), `board.json` (objects, z-order), and `assets/<sha256>.<ext>`.
  Versioned JSON Schema published in `docs/spec/chalk-format.md`.

## Smallest useful first build (Q5) — "rescue and view"

The standalone app retired today (2026-10-16), and unmigrated legacy boards
are being deleted. The most valuable first deliverable is therefore **turning
Full Export ZIPs into open, durable, editable files**. A full editor can come
later.

**M0: format + importer + CLI (no UI)**
1. `chalk-format` schema v0: board, group, stroke (points, width, widths[],
   color, tool, brush, sourceOutline), image, unsupported.
2. Importer per `docs/research/import-feasibility.md`, with an import report.
3. CLI: `chalksmith import <export.zip> -o board.chalk`,
   `chalksmith render board.chalk -o out.svg|png`, `chalksmith inspect <zip>`.
4. Synthetic fixtures: a small generator script writes fake export ZIPs
   covering pen, highlighter, textured pen, image, nested groups, an unknown
   type, and malformed input. Golden-file tests compare imported JSON and
   rendered SVG.
5. Private, local-only acceptance check against a real export: object and
   point counts match, and the rendered SVG overlays the original
   within tolerance. The result is recorded in `private/`, not committed.

**M1: viewer/editor app (Tauri)**
Open `.chalk` and Whiteboard ZIP, pan/zoom, select/move/delete groups, pen and
highlighter with pressure, eraser, undo/redo, save, export PNG/SVG/PDF.

**M2: breadth**
Text, notes, shapes, connectors, images insert, PDF insert, plus more import
types once synthetic exports are captured.

**M3: collaboration (optional)**
CRDT document, self-hosted relay.

## Proposed commits for review (nothing committed yet)

1. `chore: ignore reference and private directories`: `.gitignore`.
2. `docs: add Whiteboard architecture report, export format spec, import
   feasibility, plan`: the four files under `docs/`. Please review for any
   detail you consider private. They contain no data from private boards;
   exact figures are kept in the git-ignored `private/` folder.
3. (After you approve M0's design) `feat(core): chalk format v0 + importer +
   CLI + synthetic fixtures`.
